# watchpoint_alert_routing_rule (Resource)

A rule that routes matching alerts to extra audiences. Conditions are ANDed within a rule and ORed across rules; every matching rule contributes its targets unless it sets `stop_processing`. An alert that matches nothing (or whose targets resolve to no enabled channel) still goes to the tenant's default alert profile, so a rule can only ever add reach, never remove it. Requires the `alert_routing_rules` feature (SMB plan and above).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Anything tagged database also reaches the data team. Other rules keep being
# evaluated, so an alert can land with several audiences at once.
resource "watchpoint_alert_routing_rule" "database_to_data_team" {
  name     = "Database alerts to the data team"
  priority = 10

  conditions = [
    {
      condition_type = "MonitorTag"
      operator       = "In"
      values         = ["database", "warehouse"]
    },
  ]

  targets = [
    {
      target_type = "AlertProfile"
      target_id   = watchpoint_alert_profile.data_team.id
    },
  ]
}

# Critical alerts outside office hours page the on-call lead through a
# different escalation policy. Both conditions must match (AND), and
# stop_processing keeps lower-priority rules from adding more audiences.
resource "watchpoint_alert_routing_rule" "after_hours_critical" {
  name            = "After-hours criticals to the on-call lead"
  description     = "Weeknights 22:00-06:00, New York time"
  priority        = 20
  stop_processing = true

  conditions = [
    {
      condition_type = "Severity"
      operator       = "In"
      values         = ["Critical", "Error"]
    },
    {
      condition_type      = "TimeWindow"
      operator            = "In"
      time_zone           = "America/New_York"
      days_of_week        = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
      start_minute_of_day = 1320 # 22:00, wrapping past midnight
      end_minute_of_day   = 360  # 06:00 the next morning
    },
  ]

  targets = [
    {
      target_type = "EscalationPolicy"
      target_id   = watchpoint_escalation_policy.platform.id
    },
    {
      target_type = "Channel"
      target_id   = "chan_pagerduty_001"
    },
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Human-readable rule name.

### Optional

- `conditions` (Attributes Set) Conditions that must ALL match (AND) for the rule to fire. A rule with no conditions is a catch-all. Unordered. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--conditions))
- `description` (String) Optional description.
- `is_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is evaluated. Defaults to `true`. A disabled rule never matches.
- `owner_group_id` (String) User group (`watchpoint_user_group`) that owns this rule. A filter label only; it grants no access. The API rejects a group that does not exist in the tenant.
- `priority` (Number) Evaluation order, ascending: `100` is evaluated before `200`. Defaults to the end of the list (highest existing priority plus 10). Ties break on creation time, so the order is stable across replicas.
- `stop_processing` (Boolean) Stop evaluating lower-priority rules once this one matches. Defaults to `false`, so several rules can each contribute targets to the same alert.
- `targets` (Attributes Set) Who additionally hears about a matching alert. The channels of every matching rule are unioned and de-duplicated. Unordered. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--targets))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) Alert routing rule ID.
- `updated_at` (String) Last-update timestamp (RFC 3339).

<a id="nestedatt--conditions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `conditions`

Required:

- `condition_type` (String) What to match on. One of `MonitorTag`, `MonitorGroup`, `MonitorType`, `Severity`, `ServiceName`, `TimeWindow`.

Optional:

- `days_of_week` (Set of Number) Days the window applies to, `0` = Sunday through `6` = Saturday. Omit for every day. `TimeWindow` only. Unordered.
- `end_minute_of_day` (Number) Local minute of day the window closes, `0`-`1439`, exclusive. An end below the start wraps past midnight and belongs to the day it opened on, so a Friday 22:00-06:00 window still matches at 02:00 on Saturday. Equal start and end mean the full 24 hours, which is how a day-of-week-only rule is written. `TimeWindow` only.
- `operator` (String) How `values` is compared against the alert. `In` / `NotIn` are case-insensitive exact membership, `Contains` / `NotContains` are substring tests. Every operator is evaluated against the whole candidate set (a monitor has many tags), so `NotIn` means none of them is listed. For a `TimeWindow`, `In` means inside the window and `NotIn` outside it. Defaults to `In`.
- `start_minute_of_day` (Number) Local minute of day the window opens, `0`-`1439` (`540` is 09:00). Omit for `0`. `TimeWindow` only.
- `time_zone` (String) IANA zone id the window is evaluated in, for example `America/New_York`. Required for `TimeWindow` (an unknown id is rejected), ignored otherwise.
- `values` (Set of String) Candidate values to compare against, unordered. Required for every `condition_type` except `TimeWindow`, which ignores it. Sent to the API as a comma-separated list, so a value containing a comma cannot be expressed.


<a id="nestedatt--targets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targets`

Required:

- `target_id` (String) Id of the alert profile, channel or escalation policy. This is deliberately not a foreign key server-side: a target pointing at something that was deleted contributes nothing rather than taking the rule down with it.
- `target_type` (String) One of `AlertProfile` (all of that profile's enabled channels), `Channel` (one channel on any of the tenant's profiles), or `EscalationPolicy` (overrides the policy the alert would have escalated through; only the first one in priority order is used).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import watchpoint_alert_routing_rule.database_to_data_team arr_001
```
